findings.title: Possible crash when destinationCalendar is empty for Google Meet events
findings.body: The code destructures the first element of evt.destinationCalendar (falling back to an empty array) and then accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null or empty, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined, so a booking with location integrations:google:meet and no destination calendar throws a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video as the previous evt.destinationCalendar?.integration check did.

findings.title: updateLocation creates booking references losing externalCalendarId and credentialId
findings.body: updateLocation now maps externalCalendarId from result.externalId and credentialId from result.credentialId, but CalendarManager.updateEvent's returned EventResult never sets either field (unlike createEvent which was updated to set them). editLocation.handler persists these referencesToCreate via references.create, so after a location change the new calendar booking reference has undefined externalCalendarId/credentialId, breaking subsequent update/cancel lookups that rely on those fields.

findings.title: Google updateEvent can no longer resolve the destination calendar
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is falsy, selectedCalendar is computed by finding a destination calendar whose externalId equals externalCalendarId (null/undefined/empty), which can never match, so calendarId is passed as undefined to calendar.events.update. Previously it fell back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId. Updates/reschedules for Google bookings without a stored externalCalendarId will therefore fail or target no calendar instead of the booking's destination calendar.

findings.title: Google deleteEvent deletes from primary instead of destination calendar
findings.body: The same impossible find (cal.externalId === externalCalendarId when externalCalendarId is falsy) replaces the previous fallback to event.destinationCalendar.externalId. deleteEvent then falls back to 'primary', so cancelling a booking whose event lives on a non-primary destination calendar leaves the real event undeleted and may attempt deletion on the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Google createEvent uses first host's calendar email for every host's event
findings.body: createEvent correctly selects the target calendar by matching credentialId, but the organizer attendee email still uses mainHostDestinationCalendar (the first array element) regardless of credentialId. For collective events, events created on the second host's Google calendar carry the first host's externalId as organizer email, which mismatches the authenticated calendar and can be rejected by Google or show the wrong organizer.

findings.title: Lark createEvent ignores which destination credential is being processed
findings.body: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now calls createEvent once per destination calendar/credential, but Lark's createEvent still always uses the first destinationCalendar entry. For a collective event with multiple Lark hosts it will repeatedly create the event on the main host's calendar (duplicates) and never on the other hosts' calendars; its signature also ignores the new credentialId parameter added to the Calendar interface.

findings.title: Office365 createEvent ignores which destination credential is being processed
findings.body: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now calls createEvent once per destination calendar/credential, but Office365's createEvent still always uses the first destinationCalendar entry for the events URL. For a collective event with multiple Office365 hosts it will repeatedly create the event on the main host's calendar (duplicates) and never on the other hosts' calendars.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent ignores which destination credential is being processed
findings.body: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now calls createEvent once per destination calendar/credential, but the CalDAV/iCal base service still filters calendars by only the first destinationCalendar entry. For a collective event with multiple CalDAV hosts it will repeatedly create the event on the main host's calendar (duplicates) and never on the other hosts' calendars.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation issues duplicate delete calls per calendar reference
findings.body: The new outer loop iterates over every calendar reference, and inside the recurring branch it again iterates over all of the user's calendar credentials and all updated bookings, picking only the first calendar reference of each. With multiple hosts/references (the collective case this PR adds) the same recurring events are deleted multiple times (references x credentials), causing redundant API calls and spurious 404/410 errors that can surface as cancellation failures.
